subject: Discovery recap & PoC plan: observability, evals, and rollout guardrails
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@finservco.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.inference>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference>
Date: Sat, 7 Nov 2026 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: Recap: Observability & evals discovery — next steps

Hi Alex —

Great to meet you and Priya today. Thanks for walking us through where FinServCo is on model infra and the production concerns you called out. Below is a concise recap of what we heard, success criteria you called out, and proposed next steps for a lightweight PoC. Please reply with any corrections.

Key pain points (as discussed)
- Lack of token-level observability: hard to tie latency/cost to specific prompts and model variants.
- Regression risk from model swaps / quantization: no reliable golden-prompt regression guardrails today.
- Rollouts are manual and slow: want automated canaries and rollback triggers tied to evals.
- Traceability for compliance/audit: need request/response trace along with user-id mapping retained for 90 days.

Current stack (what you told us)
- Model hosts: internal Sagemaker endpoints (some fine-tuned Llama-family models).
- Orchestration: custom Node.js service + Redis cache.
- Monitoring: Datadog for infra, homegrown app metrics. No token-level traces today.
- CI: unit tests + nightly integration tests (no eval-driven regression checks).

Success criteria (initial)
- Observability: per-route P95 latency and cost-per-1k-token breakdown surfaced in a dashboard within PoC window.
- Evals: 50 golden prompts + automated regression alerts on critical prompts (failing if semantic drift > threshold).
- Rollouts: canary rollout with automatic rollback if regression alert fires or error-rate delta > 2x baseline.
- Compliance: request/response trace retained 90 days, exportable for audits.

PoC proposal (3-week plan)
1) Week 1 — Ingest & tracing hooks: instrument one route + attach token-level traces, sample KV cache heatmap.
2) Week 2 — Dashboards & golden prompts: deploy dashboard (latency/cost/route), upload golden prompt set and run baseline evals.
3) Week 3 — Rollout guardrails: configure canary policy + automatic rollback rules tied to eval results.

Deliverables we’ll provide
- PoC scope doc (attached) + milestone checklist.
- Dash template for FinServCo (PNG attached).
- Example golden prompts CSV (attached) and evaluation harness.

Next steps / asks from you
- Confirm scope and the single route to instrument for PoC (API name / path).
- Share an infra contact (SRE) who can approve IAM access for our tracing helper.
- Provide a sample of 10 high-priority prompts (we can expand to 50 during PoC).

Proposed follow-up: 30-min technical sync week of Nov 16 to kick off instrumentation. I’ll send a calendar invite with time options.

Thanks — looking forward to running this with you.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Internal: FinServCo PoC checklist + roles

Team —

Notes from call and internal alignment:
- Priority route /api/v1/assist; must support per-request metadata (user_id, request_id).
- Risk areas: PII in prompts — we need to propose a redaction/field-mask flow for compliance.
- SDK hooks: We’ll supply a small tracing helper (NodeJS) that emits token-level spans to a secure collection endpoint; SRE must approve egress to that endpoint.

Proposed test cases for week 2 evals:
- Regression check: run golden prompts and compare semantic similarity using embedding cosine; alert if median similarity drops > 8 points vs baseline.
- Latency: ensure p95 token latency on canary < 250ms for assistant route.
- Cost delta: cost/1k tokens should not increase more than 15% vs baseline without executive approval.

I attached the PoC scope doc we’ll send to the customer and a dashboard mock.

Action items (assigned)
- Hannah: confirm calendar times with Alex/Priya for week of Nov 16.
- Neha: draft the short encryption/retention writeup for Alex’s legal team.
- Dev: prepare tracing helper and minimal IAM steps doc.

We should be able to start instrumentation within 3 business days of IAM approval.

—Dev
